rounds.response:
calcprographics.dll as the faulting module points to the app’s rendering/graphics layer, so it’s likely either a CalcPro bug or an interaction between CalcPro and your GPU/driver.  
First confirm whether you have only integrated graphics or also a discrete GPU, then update/reinstall the relevant GPU drivers (both Intel/AMD/NVIDIA if hybrid) and retry.  
Force CalcPro to use the other adapter via Settings > System > Display > Graphics/Graphics performance preference → add CalcPro.exe → Options → choose Power saving (integrated) or High performance (discrete), then test filtering and note which adapter reproduces/avoids the crash.  
If it still fails, run the file on another PC (or do a clean boot), and collect a crash dump (ProcDump or enable Windows Error Reporting) plus the Event Viewer entry and CalcPro logs (%appdata%\CalcPro\logs) so you can attach them when filing a bug with CalcPro support.

rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Providing formatting guidance**

I want to guide the user on how to handle formatting issues safely. First, it’s important to back up the file before making changes. Next, remove conditional formatting rules by going to Conditional Formatting > Manage Rules, selecting the rules for the sheet or specific cells, and deleting unwanted rules. **Suggesting non-destructive methods**

I want to share a non-destructive way to handle formatting issues. First, copy the column to a new one using Paste Special → Values, which will remove the conditional formatting while keeping the text. rounds.response:
Make a backup copy first, then try these steps one at a time and test filtering after each.  
1) Open CalcPro’s Conditional Formatting/Manage Rules dialog, set it to show rules for the sheet or the current selection, select any rules that reference that column or range and delete them.  
2) Select the whole column and use Format/Clear Formats (or Home → Clear) or apply the Normal/Default cell style from the Styles panel to remove leftover direct styles.  
3) If you want a non‑destructive check, copy the column to a new column and Paste Special → Values only (this preserves text but strips conditional formatting/styles), then filter the new column.  
If it still crashes after those steps, save a minimal copy containing just a few problematic rows plus the problematic column and attach it with your Event Viewer entry when filing a bug.
